scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: Two lighting conditions
scenes.caption: Asha tests the same prototype on two supplied groups: bright images and dim images. Each group has eight examples. The comparison will show whether one overall score hides a difference between conditions.
scenes.dialogue: Whose examples and which conditions did we miss?

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: The average hides a gap
scenes.caption: The model gets seven of eight bright examples correct, but only three of eight dim examples correct. The gap warrants investigation. It does not, by itself, prove that lighting is the only cause.
scenes.dialogue: A difference is a clue, not a complete explanation.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Representation and proxies
scenes.caption: A collection can miss relevant conditions. An irrelevant background mark can also become a proxy the model relies on. Compare controlled examples where possible, collect suitable varied data and keep a human fallback for cases the model cannot handle.
scenes.dialogue: Check what the model is responding to.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Interpret the gap
scenes.caption: Choose what follows from the supplied bright and dim results. Avoid claiming that every dim image fails, that the model is universally accurate, or that one small comparison proves a cause.
scenes.dialogue: Say exactly what this comparison supports.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: A better plan
scenes.caption: The team proposes a separate, varied collection across lighting conditions and a fresh evaluation pack. It tests background changes carefully and routes uncertain cases to a person. It preserves the original results instead of quietly replacing failures with easy examples.
scenes.dialogue: Improve coverage without hiding the first result.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Enter the lab
scenes.caption: Calculate errors by group, inspect a controlled background change and choose a proportionate collection and review plan. State the remaining uncertainty and avoid treating correlation as proof of cause.
scenes.dialogue: Let us make missing coverage visible.
